requirement: Give a LangGraph-like chat graph durable per-conversation memory, so each thread_id resumes its own history and stored checkpoints cannot be corrupted by callers.
skeleton: A thread_id_of config helper, a MemorySaver storing deep-copied snapshots per thread with get, put and history, and a ChatGraph that resumes, appends a turn, checkpoints and counts snapshots.
caption: A LangGraph-style MemorySaver checkpointer written in the standard library with copy, collections.abc and typing and no third-party imports. thread_id_of reads config configurable thread_id, treating a missing or None configurable as empty, and raises ValueError unless it is a non-empty string. MemorySaver keeps a per-thread list: put appends a deepcopy of the state, get returns a deepcopy of the latest snapshot or None, and history returns deep copies oldest first. ChatGraph.invoke resumes from get or starts with no messages and zero turns, appends the user message and the reply computed from the messages so far, increments turns, puts the new state and returns it; snapshot_count is the history length. The fixture asserts resumption, thread isolation, that tampering never reaches stored snapshots, ordered history, and ValueError for bad thread ids.

plan.intent: Keep separate memory for each user conversation
constraints: A missing, empty or non-string thread_id raises ValueError
Each thread resumes only its own latest checkpoint
Snapshots are deep-copied on put, get and history
Every turn appends a new checkpoint in order
A new thread starts empty and get returns None

rationale.teaches: Key checkpoints by configurable.thread_id, append snapshots instead of overwriting, and deep-copy at every boundary so stored state is immutable.
rationale.why: Sharing references lets a caller silently rewrite a conversation's past, and loose thread ids merge unrelated users into one history.

ops.docstring: A LangGraph-style in-memory checkpointer keyed by thread_id.

candidates.why_wrong: The caller's state object is stored by reference and later edits rewrite the checkpoint.
get returns the stored snapshot itself, so mutating the result corrupts the thread.
Empty strings and integers are accepted as thread ids and share checkpoints.
Each put replaces the thread's history, so only the latest checkpoint survives.
A configurable value of None crashes with AttributeError instead of ValueError.
